## Household and background

Priya Raman (born June 20, 1985 — 40) is single with no dependents and owns a small house at 8 Windmere Court in Anytown. She manages the front office at Brightside Dental Partners: one W-2, box 1 wages $41,268.00, box 2 federal withholding $6,930.00 — higher than usual because of what happened in March.

That month her septic system failed, and she withdrew $12,460.00 from her traditional IRA at Keystone Trust to pay for the replacement. She is 40, no exception applies, and nothing was rolled back in — so the full amount is both taxable income (line 4b) and subject to the 10% additional tax on early distributions. She declined withholding on the withdrawal itself and instead asked payroll to take an extra $135 per paycheck for the rest of the year to cover the tax.

## Interview

**Q.** How old were you when you took the money out, and did any of it go back into an IRA within 60 days?

**A.** I was 39 turning 40, and no — it all went to the septic contractor.

**Q.** Does any exception apply — disability, high unreimbursed medical bills, a first-home purchase, higher education, a levy?

**A.** No. It was a house repair, and I'm healthy and out of school — the 1099-R even shows code 1.

**Q.** Have you ever made nondeductible IRA contributions?

**A.** No — every contribution was deducted, so the whole withdrawal is taxable.

**Q.** Why is box 4 on the 1099-R zero?

**A.** I turned down the custodian's withholding and raised my paycheck withholding by $135 a pay period instead — that's why box 2 on my W-2 is high.

**Q.** Any dependents? Could anyone claim you as a dependent? Are you blind, disabled, or a student? A U.S. citizen all year?

**A.** No to all of those, and yes — citizen all year.
